domain: Islamic Theology / Philosophy of Language / Political Authority
topic_summary: Analysis of the Mu'tazilite-Ash'arite theological dispute over whether the Qur'an is created (makhlūq) or uncreated (ghayr makhlūq) divine speech. The dispute centers on the ontological status of revelation and its implications for prophetic authority, scriptural hermeneutics, rational theology, and state doctrinal enforcement, crystallized during the 9th-century mihna (inquisition) under Abbasid caliph al-Ma'mun.

key_entities: Mu'tazilite school (rationalist theology; Qur'an as created)
Ash'arite school (traditionalist synthesis; Qur'an as uncreated eternal speech)
Abbasid caliphate (state enforcer of doctrinal orthodoxy during mihna)
Ahmad ibn Hanbal (jurist; resisted mihna; martyred traditionalist icon)
al-Ma'mun (caliph 813-833; imposed created-Qur'an doctrine via inquisition)
Qur'an itself (fixed revealed text; disputed ontological substrate)
key_tensions: Divine transcendence (tanzīh) vs divine immanence in scripture (taqlīd literalism)
Rational theology (kalām) vs transmitted tradition (naql) as interpretive authority
State enforcement of doctrine vs scholarly interpretive pluralism

axiom_contradictions.basis: No single coherent metaphysical framework can hold both 'revelation is coeternal divine attribute' and 'revelation is temporal created artifact.' Accepting uncreated status requires treating the Qur'an as ontologically equivalent to God's knowledge/will (divine attributes); accepting created status requires locating it in the category of temporal existents subject to divine creative act. These are mutually exclusive ontic categories.

The axioms do NOT contradict (both hold Qur'an as created), but the enforcement mechanism transforms the constraint type: pure rationalist reading treats creation-doctrine as conclusion of theological reasoning accessible to scholarly debate; state-enforced reading converts it into loyalty oath backed by coercion, foreclosing the debate the rationalist axiom presupposes. A pluralist framework could hold both the metaphysical claim and reject state enforcement, but no framework coherently holds 'doctrine established by rational persuasion' and 'doctrine established by inquisition threat' as compatible methods simultaneously.
